design_rationale:
WORKLOG / DOSSIER — dental_ppo_member_services task 1 (env_0070), rework round 3. Frozen time 2026-06-16 10:15:00 PDT.

[Step 0 draw] draw_counts.py --task 1: three prerequisite problems, factor counts [4, 5, 5, 6]. The claim appeal takes 4, the prior-level and new-plan-wait reprocessing rules 5 each, the grace-period reprocessing rule 6.

[Scope] Claimed here: dental_ext_claim_appeal_dispute -> file_claim_appeal_86dbcb40 (owner=user), dental_ext_upgrade_denial_reprocess -> reprocess_upgrade_denial_9a74d03b, dental_ext_grace_denial_reprocess -> reprocess_grace_denial_4c0e9d17, dental_ext_upgrade_paid_reprocess -> reprocess_upgrade_paid_line_3fd2b6c9. Task 0 claims the initial-wait reprocessing and the estimate request. A group second-level claim appeal is the appeal shape the blueprint's appeal gates admit.

[Why a good test] Corinne Abernathy asks only to file the second-level appeal of the porcelain crown on tooth 14 (claim D71-260312-3402, DOS 2026-03-10, out of network), denied DENIED_WAITING_PERIOD on 2026-03-20 and upheld at the first level on 2026-04-29. Her group (Delgado Marine Supply) moved from Value 1000 to Classic 1250 at its 2025-07-01 plan year, so crowns (not covered by Value) carry Classic's 12-month late-entrant wait counted from 2025-07-01. Her DentalCare DHMO 315 ran 2022-05-01 to 2025-05-31, the day before her group coverage began on 2025-06-01: 37 months. Three corrections stand open on her record: the 2025-12-29 amalgam (received 2026-01-12, decided 2026-01-21), paid at Value's 60% inside Classic's new 6-month basic wait and booked to benefit year 2026, its decision year, where it took the last 5.00 of the 2026 deductible (the 2025-12-02 composite paid at the prior level was appealed and is settled through its appeal); the 2026-01-20 crown on tooth 3 denied as not eligible while the group account was only in its grace period (cured by the 2026-01-28 remittance); and the appealed crown itself.

[Problem tree] root dental_ext_claim_appeal_dispute (user). Edges: (1) root -> dental_ext_upgrade_denial_reprocess, value_input, gate d_paid, state form: "The amount in dispute on a claim appeal is fixed only after the decision under appeal no longer stands denied for the new waiting period that followed a plan change, where the person's earlier Cascade DHMO coverage has already served that waiting period." Skipping it gives 160.0 instead of 74.0. (2) new-plan-wait -> dental_ext_grace_denial_reprocess, value_input, gate ded_room: "A reprocessed new-plan-wait line's patient share is fixed only after the person's most recently decided line denied as not eligible, when it is dated earlier than this line in the same benefit year on a date on which the enrollment was in force while its funding billing account was in a premium grace period, has been reprocessed." Skipping it gives 1001.0 instead of 999.0 (the earlier-dated correction takes the 5.00 of the 2026 deductible that step 17 reopens; the 2026-01-07 palliative visit took 45.00). (3) grace-period -> dental_ext_upgrade_paid_reprocess, value_input, gate ded_room: "A reprocessed grace-period line's patient share is fixed only after the person's most recently decided paid basic- or major-class line, when it is booked to this line's benefit year although its date of service falls in an earlier one and was paid at a prior plan's coinsurance for a service whose new waiting period the person's earlier Cascade DHMO coverage has already served, has been reprocessed." Skipping it gives 999.0 instead of 1001.0: the amalgam's 5.00 stays on the 2026 deductible, so the grace-period line takes none. Each state names exactly one resolving write: only the new-plan-wait rule rebooks a waiting-period denial dated after a plan change, only the grace-period rule rebooks a not-eligible denial inside coverage, only the prior-level rule rebooks a paid line at a prior plan's coinsurance. The appeal names the line its first-level filing named; the rule and the tool both say so, so the reprocessed decision's new id is not the appealed line.

[Seed realism and ledgers] Delgado Marine Supply holds group contract G-7104482 (Cascade Group Dental & Vision 20-49), Classic 1250 offered from the 2025-07-01 plan year at 32.40 / 63.05 / 67.55 / 102.20 with a rate guarantee to 2026-06-30. Corinne was added as a late entrant effective 2025-06-01 (reported 2025-05-13). The list-bill account bills the contract rate times the census by tier: the June 2025 invoice (issued 2025-05-02, prior plan year's Value 1000 rates 28.95 / 56.30 / 60.35 / 91.25, census 8/3/3/5) was 1037.80, a supplementary 28.95 on 2025-05-14 added her June month (one remittance of 1066.75 paid both), and from July 2025 every invoice bills 9/3/3/5 at the Classic rates = 1194.40; remittances paid each month, the January 2026 premium only on 2026-01-28 as a grace cure (grace period from 2026-01-01, 31 days), the July 2026 invoice is open (balance 1194.40). Her DHMO was funded by an individual direct-bill account: 37 monthly invoices of 15.40 (DHMO 315 member_only) from May 2022 to May 2025, each paid by card (the first as binder), closed 2025-06-05 on her confirmed closure request of 2025-06-03. She has coverage through a part-time employer (Harborview Marine Employees Dental Plan), which pays first under the longer-coverage rule; Classic coordinates by non-duplication. History: 2025-08-19 and 2026-02-17 preventive visits paid at 90% less the primary payments; the 2025-12-02 composite on tooth 30 paid at Value's 60% (alternate benefit, deductible 50.00, appeal upheld 2026-02-04); a 2026-01-07 palliative visit whose 45.00 allowance went to the deductible (decided 2026-01-14, before the amalgam, which then took the remaining 5.00); the 2026-02-17 bitewings were denied for the 12-month interval and that denial went through both appeal levels (upheld 2026-03-27 and 2026-04-22).

[Computation 1, step 17, prior-level reprocessing, expected 45.0] amalgam D2150 tooth 4, billed 150.00 below allowed 165.00; 37 months serve the 6-month new basic wait from 2025-07-01, so Classic's out-of-network basic 70% applies; booked to 2025, the year of its date of service; deductible 0.00 (the 2025 deductible was met by the 2025-12-02 line; its replaced decision's 5.00 posting to 2026 is reversed); (150.00 - 0.00) x 70% = 105.00 less 45.00 primary = 60.00; share 150.00 - 60.00 - 45.00 = 45.00. Baselines: credit 0 -> 60.0 (stays at the recorded 60%); in-network 80% -> 30.0; allowed 165.00 -> 34.5; no coordination -> 0.0; no primary credit -> 90.0; all -> 51.0.

[Computation 2, step 19, grace-period reprocessing, expected 1001.0] crown D2750 tooth 3, received the day after service; 37 months serve the 12-month new major wait; out-of-network major 40%; molar-crown alternate 965.00; deductible 5.00 (45.00 taken by the palliative visit; the amalgam's 5.00 reversed by step 17); (965.00 - 5.00) x 40% = 384.00 less 310.00 = 74.00; share 1385.00 - 74.00 - 310.00 = 1001.00. Baselines: credit 0 -> 1075.0; in-network 50% -> 905.0; allowed 1150.00 -> 927.0; no coordination -> 691.0; share from the allowed amount -> 766.0; no primary credit -> 1311.0; all -> 1150.0.

[Computation 3, step 21, new-plan-wait reprocessing, expected 999.0] crown D2750 tooth 14; 37 months serve the wait; 40%; alternate 965.00; deductible 0.00 (met by the palliative visit and step 19); 386.00 less 300.00 = 86.00; share 1385.00 - 86.00 - 300.00 = 999.00. Baselines: credit 0 -> 1085.0; 50% -> 902.5; allowed -> 925.0; no coordination -> 699.0; no primary credit -> 1299.0; all -> 1385.0.

[Computation 4, step 23, claim appeal, expected 74.0] decision under appeal = the corrected 2026-03-10 decision (paid 86.00); requested allowance 1150.00 (the contested alternate reduction); requested deductible 0.00 (50.00 met by other lines, the decision's own posting none); 40%; 460.00 less 300.00 = 160.00; dispute 160.00 - 86.00 = 74.00; due 2026-07-16 (30 days). Baselines: the decision's allowance 965.00 -> 0.0; 50% -> 189.0; no coordination -> 374.0; credit 0 -> 0.0; all -> 0.0.

[Stamps and near misses] The two denied crowns carry no allowance-used stamp; the amalgam's original decision used the 165.00 allowed amount, not the 150.00 the correction uses. Near misses: the 2025-12-02 composite (paid at the prior level but under appeal, and decided earlier than the amalgam); the amalgam's recorded benefit year 2026 (the correction is booked to 2025, the year of its date of service); the 2026-01-07 palliative visit (paid at Classic's level in a later benefit year); the bitewing appeals and the composite's appeal (an earlier first-level decision on another line, and a second-level filing that is not on the crown); the preventive paid lines are not basic or major; the 2025 postings belong to another benefit year.

[Persona] Corinne raises only the second-level appeal; she agrees to any correction only when the representative raises it, and gives the other-coverage name only when asked.


[Round 3] D2: the round-2 state gate (grace-period <- prior-level) is gone; the prior-level correction now bears weight as a value edge: its line, dated 2025-12-29 but booked to 2026, holds 5.00 of the 2026 deductible, and its correction (booked to 2025, the year of its date of service, as the tool's benefit-year argument records) reopens that 5.00 for the grace-period line. Every prerequisite sentence now names the resolver's own selection (the most recently decided line of that kind) and the same benefit year, so no line the resolver cannot reach keeps a gate shut (the appealed 2025 composite is outside the sentence: it is not the latest decided paid line and is booked to 2025). D3: the pediatric crossing has one reading (share limited first, plan payment = allowance less the limited share); no pediatric person here.

[Round 6, seed only] src-2: her DHMO 315 enrollment is assigned to the primary care dentist Ana R. Okafor, DMD of Lincoln Avenue Dental Care (active Cascade DHMO Primary Care Dentist Agreement, general dentist, private practice, WA; application 2016-01-11, approved after site review 2016-03-28, in network from 2016-04-01, the first of the month after approval; recredentialed every 36 months, most recently on 2025-03-24, before the 2025-03-28 due date, so the next due date is 2028-03-24; liability 1,000,000 / 3,000,000), read by two gold look-ups; every claim line of hers is out of network and names no agreement. src-4: the prior plan year's Value 1000 group rates are now 28.95 / 56.30 / 60.35 / 91.25, so the 2025-07-01 renewal to Classic 1250 at 32.40 / 63.05 / 67.55 / 102.20 rises 11.9 / 12.0 / 11.9 / 12.0 percent, within the 12 percent renewal rate cap of the 20-49 segment; the June 2025 invoices and remittance are re-priced at those rates. No scored value moved; the gold writes shifted two steps later because of the two added reads.

[Round 7, seed only] E1: each provider agreement now records its original credentialing application date and the effective date the approval produced (first of the month after the original decision); the credentialing decision date, recredential due date, licence and liability fields are the ones the latest recredentialing refreshed, the only fields that event writes. Each practice profile was opened before its first application.
user_scenario: You are Corinne Abernathy, a 46-year-old purchasing coordinator at Delgado Marine Supply in Tacoma, Washington: direct, a little tired of paperwork, and polite. You are calling Cascade Mutual Dental & Vision about the dental PPO you have through work. Your member ID is CM71448203, your date of birth is 1979-06-11 and your ZIP code is 98406; give them when asked. In March an out-of-network dentist put a porcelain crown on your upper-left back molar (tooth 14) and the claim was denied for a waiting period. You appealed, and on April 29 you got a letter saying the first-level appeal was upheld. You were on Cascade's DentalCare DHMO for three years until you joined your employer's plan in June 2025, with no break in between, and your employer's plan was changed to a richer plan in July 2025. You want to file that second-level appeal today, yourself, during this call, and you want the representative to tell you exactly what to enter, including the amount in dispute and the date the decision is due. You also have dental coverage through a part-time job, Harborview Marine Employees Dental Plan, which pays first; mention it only if asked. You do not know any dollar figures or plan rules and do not guess them. If the representative says something on your claims has to be corrected or reprocessed before the appeal, you tell them that's fine and to go ahead. When you have the appeal reference number you thank them and end the call.

base_preconditions.condition: A first-level appeal may be filed no later than the appeal filing window after the adverse determination date shown on the Explanation of Benefits.
A second-level appeal exists only for group enrollments, and may be filed no later than the second-level window after the first-level appeal decision.
A second-level appeal exists only for group enrollments, and may be filed no later than the second-level window after the first-level appeal decision.

Only an adverse determination can be appealed: a line with a DENIED_* remark, a line paid with PAID_ALTERNATE_BENEFIT or PAID_REDUCED_ANNUAL_MAX, a reprocessed line, or an estimate line with an ESTIMATE_* remark other than ESTIMATE_COVERED.
Only one filing per appealed line per level may exist.

temporal_feasibility.condition: A first-level appeal may be filed no later than the appeal filing window after the adverse determination date shown on the Explanation of Benefits.

temporal_basis.counting_rule: The filing window is appeal_filing_window_days counted in calendar days from the adjudicated_date of the appealed line (or the issued_date of the appealed estimate line), and a filing received on the last day of the window is timely.

edges.condition: The latest decision on the appealed line's claim number and line number is a reprocessed (adjusted) decision, no longer the DENIED_WAITING_PERIOD denial.
edges.policy_source: The amount in dispute on a claim appeal is fixed only after the decision under appeal no longer stands denied for the new waiting period that followed a plan change, where the person's earlier Cascade DHMO coverage has already served that waiting period.

unresolved_at_frozen_time.why_false: The latest decision on claim D71-260312-3402 line 1 is still the 2026-03-20 DENIED_WAITING_PERIOD denial, although 37 DHMO months serve the 12-month new wait.

edges.condition: The person's most recently decided DENIED_NOT_ELIGIBLE line, dated earlier in the same benefit year inside the cured grace period of the group list bill, has a reprocessed (adjusted) decision with its deductible posted.
edges.policy_source: A reprocessed new-plan-wait line's patient share is fixed only after the person's most recently decided line denied as not eligible, when it is dated earlier than this line in the same benefit year on a date on which the enrollment was in force while its funding billing account was in a premium grace period, has been reprocessed.

unresolved_at_frozen_time.why_false: The 2026-01-20 crown (the person's most recently decided DENIED_NOT_ELIGIBLE line, dated earlier in 2026 than the 2026-03-10 crown) still stands denied although the group account was only in grace and was cured on 2026-01-28.
unresolved_at_frozen_time.flips_to_true_by: The corrected grace-period decision takes the 5.00 of the 2026 deductible that the prior-level correction reopened, so the new-plan-wait line takes 0.00 and its patient share becomes 999.0.

edges.condition: The person's most recently decided paid basic or major line, dated in the earlier benefit year but booked to the grace-period line's benefit year at the prior plan's coinsurance, has a reprocessed (adjusted) decision booked to the benefit year of its date of service, and the deductible and maximum postings the replaced decision made to the grace-period line's benefit year are reversed.
edges.policy_source: A reprocessed grace-period line's patient share is fixed only after the person's most recently decided paid basic- or major-class line, when it is booked to this line's benefit year although its date of service falls in an earlier one and was paid at a prior plan's coinsurance for a service whose new waiting period the person's earlier Cascade DHMO coverage has already served, has been reprocessed.

unresolved_at_frozen_time.why_false: The 2025-12-29 filling (the person's most recently decided paid basic line, decided 2026-01-21) still stands paid at Value 1000's 60% and booked to 2026, holding 5.00 of the 2026 deductible, although its date of service falls in 2025 and 37 DHMO months serve the new basic wait.
unresolved_at_frozen_time.flips_to_true_by: The filling's corrected decision is booked to 2025 at 70% and its 2026 deductible posting of 5.00 is reversed, so 5.00 of the 2026 deductible is open again for the grace-period line, which then takes it (patient share 1001.0 instead of 999.0).

prerequisite_closure.order_uniqueness: The tree is a chain (appeal <- new-plan-wait <- grace-period <- prior-level) and every edge is a value edge, so the order is fixed by the stated edges. Booking the grace-period line before the filling's correction leaves the 2026 deductible fully taken for it (grace-period share 999.0) and hands the reopened 5.00 to the new-plan-wait line (share 1001.0); only the stated order gives the gold figures.

the grace-period line's member_responsibility changes from 1001.0 to 999.0: without the filling's correction its 5.00 stays on the 2026 deductible, so the grace-period line takes 0.00; the corrected 2025 filling decision and its reversals are missing.
